coreRequests.want: a `tileset` field on Placement (or a multi-tileset MapDraft), so terrain.load can realise a map that mixes bw2-adastra with structures and props
coreRequests.why: `tiles.buildInstances(scene, slug, placements)` resolves modelId against one tileset, so a structures id put through an AdAstra draft silently draws an unrelated AdAstra model. Every scene that places an authored building has to build and dispose its own extra InstancedWorlds (src/city/structures.js). It works and costs 21 draw calls, but it is a trap every future map author will fall into once (DECISIONS #26a).

coreRequests.want: environment.lamps.add({ point:false }) — a glow-only bulb that never claims a slot in the 8-light pool
coreRequests.why: lamps.update() hands the pool to the eight bulbs nearest the camera focus, by distance alone. A lit window wants a glow quad and a small wall wash; a street lamp wants the ground pool. Today registering more than a couple of windows near the camera silently takes the PointLights away from the street lamps, so the city registers exactly two lit doorways and no window bulbs at all.
coreRequests.closedBy: environment r2 - lamps.add({ point:false }) exists and is verified in the running page (a point:false bulb at the camera focus claims no PointLight; a normal bulb two cells away takes env:lamp0; the pool stays at 8). Not yet CALLED by any scene, so city still has to pass the flag for its windows before the frame changes. DECISIONS #31h.

coreRequests.why: Every AdAstra tree is two upright cards at x=1 and z=1 and the camera never yaws (ARCHITECTURE 2.7), so the x=1 card is permanently perpendicular to the view and rasterises as a full-height sliver of canopy texture. `simulation` measured the same geometry independently (DECISIONS #29) and plants no tree at all because of it. Round 2's normal floor stops the sliver being black, but it is still a sliver.

coreRequests.want: tiles: the 22-degree normal floor can be relaxed now, and should be re-measured rather than removed.
coreRequests.why: DECISIONS #30a clamps every normal to 22 deg above the horizon because a vertical face took hemisphere fill only. Round 2 added two directional fills: an anti-sun `bounce` at 20 deg (a wall turned away from the key takes 0.94 of it) and a camera-axis `camFill` at 38 deg. A vertical face now has two real sources with direction, which is the condition the clamp was working around. ab-fills-off-8.png against city-8.png is the measurement of what the fills are worth on exactly those surfaces.

coreRequests.want: a rim/Fresnel term the environment can drive - either a shared material onBeforeCompile hook every module's materials pass through, or a rim pass in core/render.js's composite driven from the depth/normal buffers it already renders
coreRequests.why: Round 3's ranked note 4 is 'night away from lamps has no accent - it needs a rim/specular term on silhouettes' (docs/refs/03 sells its whole night on rim light along the fence posts). Every material in the frame is a MeshLambertMaterial owned by tiles and pokemon, and Lambert has no view-dependent term at all: no light I can add from environment produces a rim, because a back light gives a camera-facing card dot(N,L) < 0. This is the last defect in the night frame that environment cannot reach from its own folder.

coreRequests.want: expose shadow.radius / a PCF radius on the sun light, or switch the shadow map type per preset
coreRequests.why: core sets PCFSoftShadowMap in makeRenderer and its filter width is fixed, so tile and building shadows have a constant penumbra whatever the sun's elevation and whatever the distance from the contact point. The critic's note 3 asks for the opposite ('shrink the PCF radius near the contact point'). The projected sprite shadows in src/environment/castShadows.js do contact-harden, which makes the mismatch between the two shadow kinds visible in the same frame.

coreRequests.want: core/render.js should read config.shadowBias and config.shadowNormalBias every frame instead of once in makeSunShadow
coreRequests.why: environment recomputes both from the sun's elevation every apply() (a grazing sun needs roughly three times the normal offset a noon sun does) and has to write them straight onto three.sun.light.shadow to make them take effect. That works but it means two owners for the same two numbers.

coreRequests.want: a dialogue seam: NPC lines on `simulation.spawnNpc(spec)` (a `lines` field, echoed back by `npcs()`), or a `city` API that answers "who is on this cell" with something to say
coreRequests.why: ARCHITECTURE 5.12 lists dialogue boxes and `ui.say(text, {speaker})` is built and verified. Nothing in the tree publishes a line: city spawns thirteen walkers with routes and no script, and spawnNpc's spec carries only {trainer, species, shiny, name}. The UI can already find the NPC on the cell the trainer faces from `player()` + `npcs()`, so all that is missing is the text. Inventing it here would put content in the wrong module.

coreRequests.want: tools/shots: a way to drive input from the harness — `window.__HOOKS__.key(code, down)` or `press(dir, frames)`
coreRequests.why: The input seam is the one thing in this module a screenshot alone cannot prove: shoot.js sets a preset and a time of day but cannot press a key, so verifying that a held ArrowRight walks the trainer needed a private puppeteer script. A hook would let gauntlet.js capture a walking frame, a running frame and a menu-open frame deterministically, and would let any future module test its own key handling.

coreRequests.want: ARCHITECTURE 5.12: the wording "DOM overlay (not WebGL) at full resolution" should read "a 2-D canvas at the renderer's internal resolution (not WebGL), upscaled with the scene"
coreRequests.why: The shipped module deviates from the letter of 5.12 deliberately and the reason is in DECISIONS #34a: text laid out in CSS pixels over a 640x360 buffer upscaled x3 is the only thing on screen off the pixel grid, and it reads as a debug overlay rather than as the game. The part of 5.12 that was load-bearing — not WebGL, so the UI cannot cost draw calls — is honoured exactly (0 draws added, measured). Flagging the mismatch rather than leaving it to be read as an ignored contract.

coreRequests.want: ARCHITECTURE 4: add `catch:failed` { species, shiny, ball, odds, shakes, turn, index } to the event table
coreRequests.why: A failed catch is half of what this module does and there is no event for it. It is emitted today (nothing subscribes, so nothing breaks) because `ui` wants it for a message, `automation` wants it to count wasted balls, and `economy` may one day want it to notice a bag draining. Adding an event is a core change, so the emit ships and the table is asked to catch up.

coreRequests.want: tools/seams/run.js: a mirror check that `encounter/rolls.js catchRateFor` and `automation/fields.js catchRateFor` are the same curve, the way rule 5 checks idle/accrual against economy/pacing
coreRequests.why: Both modules need a capture rate for a species the snapshot does not carry one for, neither may import the other (ARCHITECTURE 5), so the curve exists twice. That is exactly the failure mode rule 5 was written for: economy/pacing.js had already drifted from idle/accrual.js by 55% with nothing at runtime able to notice. Sample both at BST 195/300/450/600/700 and compare.

coreRequests.want: idle: resolve closed-tab encounters through `encounter.rollAt(index, { biome, tod })` instead of `accrual.js`'s own `rollEncounter`
coreRequests.why: ARCHITECTURE 5.6/5.7 promise that a seed and an index give the same encounter whether it was rolled live or caught up offline, and today they do not: `accrual.js` picks uniformly from `tablesFor` with its own level band and its own `idle/encounter/N` stream, so index 400 is a different Pokemon in the two paths. `src/encounter/rolls.js` is a pure `(seed, index)` module with no ctx and no clock built for exactly this call, and `encounter.rollAt` is on the public API. Needs idle's owner or the integrator; encounter cannot reach into accrual.js.

coreRequests.want: ui: bind a throw to `encounter.attempt(ballId)` and a run to `encounter.flee()`
coreRequests.why: Nothing in the game throws a ball. `automation` is off by default (5.11) and there is no input path, so a live encounter is resolved as a battle and the wild leaves - walking through grass earns, but a player can never catch anything by hand. `encounter.attempt(ballId)` returns a boolean, `encounter.active()` gives the target, `encounter.bestBall()` gives economy's recommendation and `encounter.oddsFor(id)` prices any ball without spending one.

coreRequests.want: a `tileset` field on `Placement`, so one map can draw from more than one generated set
coreRequests.why: `terrain.load` builds exactly one `InstancedWorld` from `draft.tileset`, and `InstancedWorld` resolves every placement id against that set alone - so a `props` id put through an AdAstra draft silently draws AdAstra's model of the same number (DECISIONS #26a). `city` works around it with a second world built from its own layout; `hunts` now does the same through `biome.build -> extras[] -> tiles.buildInstances`. Both copies exist only because a placement cannot name its own set. Same request `city` filed; re-filed because a second module has now paid for it.

coreRequests.want: `tiles`: a catalog `footprint` that matches the geometry, or a `spills` tag on models whose bounds leave the cells they claim
coreRequests.why: Three AdAstra path tiles are catalogued 1x1 and are not: `sterr_patch` spans 0..2 on both axes (four cells) and `rot_dirtpatch` reaches x = -0.49. A scatter that trusts `w`/`h` paints over its neighbours - the first forest laid a 3-cell trail and rendered a six-cell one. `hunts/compose.js` guards it with `snug()` by re-reading `model.bounds`, which every map author would otherwise have to rediscover.

coreRequests.want: `terrain`: let `MapDraft.place` take a placement from another tileset, or expose `draft.reserve(model, cx, cz)` for footprint + collision without a placement
coreRequests.why: A scene that wants a prop from `props` has to hand-roll the collision and footprint bookkeeping `draft.place` already does, because calling `place` would emit a placement with the wrong tileset's id. `hunts/props.js` reimplements it in nine lines and `city/structures.js` reimplements it again. Strictly weaker than the `Placement.tileset` request above and worth doing only if that one is rejected.

coreRequests.want: pokemon / core render: a sprite billboard's transparent margin should not take light from a nearby PointLight
coreRequests.why: A party member standing inside a lamp pool grows a pale rounded rectangle the exact size of its own quad - the billboard's own transparent border, lit. It follows the sprite between camera framings rather than staying with the geometry near it, and `city`'s night shots at intensity 2.0 / radius 12 show none of it, so it is a near-field candela threshold rather than a broken material. `hunts` mitigated it by halving every cave light and roughly doubling its reach (same light on the floor, much less at the sprite); the halo shrinks and does not go. Visible in docs/progress/hunts/r1/cave-terrace.png and cave-21.png. Likely wants an alphaTest on the sprite material, or the margin's alpha clamped to zero at atlas build.

coreRequests.want: environment: the cave preset's warm fog and saturation, and its sun 5.20 inside a sealed room
coreRequests.why: Same cave map, same seven bulbs, same albedo tints, only CAVE.preset swapped cave -> interior: mean saturation 0.963 -> 0.441 and luminance sd 25.1 -> 38.3, against docs/refs/02's 0.194 / 53.7 and 04's 0.773 / 37.9. Grading the floor albedo by distance-to-bulb - everything hunts can reach - moved saturation by 0.003, so fog 0x4a2f18 at density 0.040 / boost 1.35 plus saturation 1.30 is about 170x the lever this module has. The interior preset is not the answer either (it crushes 57.7% in a room with no windows); the cave wants interior's fog density with cave's exposure. Separately the preset keeps sun 5.20 at every hour, so an enclosed cave draws hard black directional shadows at 21:00 from a sun that is not there. Shots: docs/progress/hunts/r2/ctl-cave-envinterior2-12.png vs c2-cave-12.png.

coreRequests.want: environment: the forest preset's night, and the depth of the moon's shadow map
coreRequests.why: Not the whole of the forest's black night - most of that was this module's canopy and is fixed - but two measurable slices of it. (a) The same forest map at tod 21 under the *meadow* preset crushes 58.4% instead of 68.6%, so hemi x0.78 / fogDensity x1.75 / vignette +0.08 costs ~10 points of the frame. (b) --envNoShadow=1 on the round-2 forest moves it from 51.4% crushed to 36.3% and doubles p50, so the moon's shadow map alone is ~15 points; --envNoCast=1 is only 1.2. For scale: an open biome under this ramp already matches the reference night (meadow-21 11.9% crushed / p50 31.4 against docs/refs/03's 10.5% / 33.2), so the ramp is right and it is the shadow depth at night that is too deep. Shots: docs/progress/hunts/r2/ctl-forest-envmeadow-21.png, ctl-forest-21-noshadow.png, ctl-forest-21-nocast.png, ctl-meadow-21.png, ctl-coast-21.png.

coreRequests.want: `idle` to stop accruing while `config.timeFrozen` is set, so a showcase capture is a pure function of the URL
coreRequests.why: The showcase contract (ARCHITECTURE 6.3) is 'same URL, same pixels'. Two captures of ?showcase=ui&mode=shop&tod=21&grain=0 differ in exactly 504 pixels in one 50x20 box — the money digits — because idle:tick keeps accruing through the harness's settle window. Measured control: the same pair for &mode=boxes and &mode=dex, which draw no currency, is byte-identical across all 1,440,000 pixels (max channel delta 0). So it is the balance that moves, not the renderer. The critic filed this as its issue 17a against `idle`; ui cannot fix it without lying about the wallet.

coreRequests.want: environment: a shallower sun-shadow at a low sun, or a documented decision that 0.17 transmission is the intended look
coreRequests.why: A critic scored encounter down for shadows that 'transmit 11% of the light, 3-4x deeper than the same engine's own control'. Measured with an A/B in the running page (sun.castShadow toggled off, same URL, tod 17.5, biome preset 'meadow'): sun-shadow transmission is 0.173 in encounter's showcase and 0.191 in simulation's - the two agree to 10%, so it is the rig and not the scene. The critic's 0.443 control was pokemon's painted contact-shadow decal (DECISIONS #18), which is a fixed-opacity quad and not a shadow-mapped shadow, so the two numbers were never comparable. Filing rather than working around: a scene cannot raise the fill without also raising the lit ground beside it. DECISIONS #39e.

coreRequests.want: tiles: a tall-grass model that tiles edge-to-edge, or a placement offset on Placement
coreRequests.why: `tall_grass` and `tall_grass_light` do not fill their cell, so a patch of them shows a grid of gaps whatever per-cell rotation and tint are applied - which is most of what makes a field read as a nursery at 2x. Rotation and tint (DECISIONS #39c) break the identical-rosette repeat but cannot move a plant off its own cell centre. A sub-cell offset on Placement, or a 2x2 grass model, would close it.

integratorFindings.topic: hunts' critic: 'NO HIGHLIGHT RANGE ANYWHERE — highest p99 across 41 shots is 152.2'

Measured now at tod 12: forest, cave, meadow and coast all reach p99 234, against reference 01 at 148 and 04 at 181; the city reaches 234 at noon and 210 at golden hour. No core tone-mapping change was made, because the measurement does not support one.

Percentage of pixels below luma 8 at tod 21: forest 48.93%, coast 9.14%, meadow 6.14%, cave 0.20%, against reference 03-forest-voxel-night.png at 10.5%. integratorFindings.topic: coast: the shoreline staircase with no surf (hunts' open issue #8)
integratorFindings.verdict: CONFIRMED, still present after the round-2 fix, and the cause is now pinned. Cropped the deep/shallow boundary at 2x: long axis-aligned runs meeting at right angles with no transition tile of any kind, while the sand/grass boundary one band below it scallops correctly because it is autotiled.
integratorFindings.cause: `deep = water.clone().shrink(3)` is an erosion, and eroding by 3 removes every one-cell feature, so the deep-water region is a SMOOTHED copy of the coastline — which quantised onto the grid is a clean staircase. The deep region is then laid as flat cells with no border family, so its edge is blocky whatever shape it has.
integratorFindings.triedAndReverted: fraying the deep edge after the erosion (ragged 0.5 / period 3, despeckle 4). It makes it worse: without border tiles, every frayed cell is another hard rectangle, so the edge goes from a straight staircase to floating dark-blue blocks. Looked at it, reverted it.
integratorFindings.theActualFix: bw2-adastra ships a complete 13-slot `walk_edge` family — corners, edges and inner corners — tagged `foam` and `surf`, and it is not being used on this boundary at all. The model named `sea` has no border family, so the deep water can only ever be blocky on its own; the foam belongs to the shallows and should ring the wadeable region on BOTH its edges, against the land and against the deep. That is hunts/biomes/coast.js's to make.
